A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a framework that allows us to study the transient and steady state behavior of a large family of cache replacement schemes and that we have provided guidelines on how to design replacement algorithms within the framework.
we provide an accurate, efficient and flexible framework to study the performance of the cache replacement algorithms within the family considered.
we have a family of cache-replacement algorithms that are easy to implement, have low computational complexity, and are able to outperform LRU in terms of hit probability.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the cache replacement algorithms that we study are simple to implement, can be tuned to achieve a good trade-off between the cache reactivities and steady-state hit probabilities, can outperform LRFU and LRU, and that they are suitable for large scale systems.
it is possible to design cache replacement algorithms that can be implemented in a very simple way, but that can outperform classical policies like LRU and FIFO.
it is possible to design cache replacement policies with a small memory footprint that can outperform LIRU in terms of hit ratio.
